27789-a-royal-prisoner.title: A Royal Prisoner
27789-a-royal-prisoner.creator: Unknown
27789-a-royal-prisoner.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Jerome Fandor, reporter on the popular newspaper, _La Capitale_, was strolling along the boulevard; he had just come from a banquet, one of those official and deadly affairs at which the guests are obliged to listen to interminable speeches. He had drowsed through the evening and at the first opportunity had managed to slip away quickly.

47229-the-merry-go-round.title: The Merry Go Round
47229-the-merry-go-round.creator: W. Somerset Maugham
47229-the-merry-go-round.description: A book by W. Somerset Maugham. Miss Dwarris loved to feel her power. During these long visits—for in a way the old lady was very hospitable—she made it her especial object to break the spirit of her guests, and it entertained her hugely to see the mildness with which were borne her extravagant demands, the humility with which every inclination was crushed.

arxiv-2106-06302.title: Enhanced Parameter Estimation with Periodically Driven Quantum Probe
arxiv-2106-06302.creator: Peter A. Ivanov
arxiv-2106-06302.description: Abstract We propose a quantum metrology protocol for measuring frequencies and weak forces based on a periodic modulating quantum Jahn-Teller system composed of a single spin interacting with two bosonic modes. We show that in the first order of the frequency drive the time-independent effective Hamiltonian describes spin-dependent interaction between the two bosonic modes.

arxiv-2204-03498.description: Abstract . Developers frequently use APIs to implement certain functionalities, such as parsing Excel Files, reading and writing text files line by line, etc. Developers can greatly benefit from automatic API usage sequence generation based on natural language queries for building applications in a faster and cleaner manner.

arxiv-2210-08618.title: M31N 1926-07c: A Recurrent Nova in M31 with a 2.8 Year Recurrence Time Facilities: Ondřejov Observatory (OND) 0.65-m, Ningbo Bureau of Education and Xinjiang Observatory Telescope (NEXT) 0.6-m, Burke-Gaffney Observatory (BGO) 0.6-m, Mount Laguna Observatory (MLO) 1.0-m.
arxiv-2210-08618.creator: Allen W. Shafter, Kamil Hornoch, Hana Kučáková, Jingyuan Zhao (赵经远), Mi Zhang (张宓), Xing Gao (高兴), John Della Costa, William A. Burris, J. Grace Clark, Marek Wolf, Petr Zasche
arxiv-2210-08618.description: Abstract The M31 recurrent nova M31N 1926-07c has had five recorded eruptions. Well-sampled light curves of the two most recent outbursts, in January of 2020 (M31N 2020-01b) and September 2022 (M31N 2022-09a), are presented showing that the photometric evolution of the two events were quite similar, with peak magnitudes of R = 17.2 ± 0.1 R=17.2\pm 0.

arxiv-2210-16583.title: In-Liquido Computation with Electrochemical Transistors and Mixed Conductors for Intelligent Bioelectronics
arxiv-2210-16583.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . Next-generation implantable computational devices require long-term stable electronic components capable of operating in, and interacting with, electrolytic surroundings without being damaged. Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) emerged as fitting candidates. However, while single devices feature impressive figures of merit, integrated circuits (ICs) immersed in a common electrolytes are hard to realize using electrochemical transistors, and there is no clear path forward for optimal top-down circuit design and high-density integration.

arxiv-2306-04012.title: Evolution of 3GPP Standards Towards True Extended Reality (XR) Support in 6G Networks
arxiv-2306-04012.creator: Ali A. Esswie, and Morris Repeta Standards & Industry Forums, Advanced Wireless Technology, Dell Technologies
arxiv-2306-04012.description: Abstract Extended reality (XR) is a key innovation of 5G-advanced and beyond networks. The diverse XR use-cases, including virtual reality, augmented reality, and mixed reality, transform the way humans interact with surrounding environments. Thus, XR technology enables true immersive experiences of novel services spanning, e.g., e-commerce, healthcare, and education, respectively.

arxiv-2309-00495.title: Nonreciprocal superconducting transport and the spin Hall effect in gyrotropic structures
arxiv-2309-00495.creator: Tim Kokkeler, I. V. Tokatly, F. Sebastián Bergeret
arxiv-2309-00495.description: Abstract The search for superconducting systems exhibiting nonreciprocal transport and, specifically, the diode effect, has proliferated in recent years. This trend has encompassed a wide variety of systems, including planar hybrid structures, asymmetric SQUIDs, and certain noncentrosymmetric superconductors. A common feature of such systems is a gyrotropic symmetry, realized on different scales and characterized by a polar vector.

arxiv-2310-19309.title: A simple quantum algorithm to efficiently prepare sparse states
arxiv-2310-19309.creator: Debora Ramacciotti, Andreea I. Lefterovici, Antonio F. Rotundo
arxiv-2310-19309.description: Abstract State preparation is a fundamental routine in quantum computation, for which many algorithms have been proposed. Among them, perhaps the simplest one is the Grover-Rudolph algorithm. In this paper, we analyse the performance of this algorithm when the state to prepare is sparse.

arxiv-2409-15681.title: El Teorema de Gelfand Naimark desde una perspectiva Categórica The Gelfand–Naimark Theorem from a Categorical Perspective
arxiv-2409-15681.creator: Sebastian Alvarez Avendaño, Breitner Ocampo, Pedro Rizzo
arxiv-2409-15681.description: Abstract The goal of this paper is to prove the categorical equivalence between the category of Hausdorff-Compact topological spaces and the category of Unital Commutative C ∗ C^{*} -algebras. This equivalence can be interpreted as a way of rewriting the well known Gelfand-Naimark Theorem [ 13 ] in a categorical language.

arxiv-2510-03164.title: Why Do We Need Warm-up? A Theoretical Perspective
arxiv-2510-03164.creator: Foivos Alimisis ∗, Rustem Islamov ∗, Aurelien Lucchi
arxiv-2510-03164.description: Abstract Learning rate warm-up – increasing the learning rate at the beginning of training – has become a ubiquitous heuristic in modern deep learning, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we provide a principled explanation for why warm-up improves training.

arxiv-2601-21253.title: CovAgent : Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation CCS: Software and its engineering Software testing and debugging
arxiv-2601-21253.creator: Wei Minn, Biniam Fisseha Demissie, Yan Naing Tun, Jiakun Liu, Mariano Ceccato, Lwin Khin Shar, David Lo
arxiv-2601-21253.description: Abstract . Automated GUI testing is crucial for ensuring the quality and reliability of Android apps. However, the efficacy of existing UI testing techniques is often limited, especially in terms of coverage. Recent studies, including the state-of-the-art, struggle to achieve more than 30% activity coverage in real-world apps.

pmc-10656188.creator: Chitra Kamath, Rachita Dhurat, Bhavika Shah, Richa Sharma, Priyanka Arun Kowe, Sachin Chamle
pmc-10656188.description: IntroductionPreviously laid down criteria for lesional stability of vitiligo are inconsistent. Longitudinal data on correlation between dermoscopic features of vitiligo and disease activity is limited.ObjectivesTo sequentially determine the dermoscopic features of vitiligo and to assess their association with the dynamic nature of the vitiligo patch.

pmc-10695996.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of traffic bottlenecks yields an early signal of heavy congestions
pmc-10695996.creator: Jinxiao Duan, Guanwen Zeng, Nimrod Serok, Daqing Li, Efrat Blumenfeld Lieberthal, Hai-Jun Huang, Shlomo Havlin
pmc-10695996.description: Heavy traffic jams are difficult to predict due to the complexity of traffic dynamics. Understanding the network dynamics of traffic bottlenecks can help avoid critical large traffic jams and improve overall traffic conditions. Here, we develop a method to forecast heavy congestions based on their early propagation stage.

pmc-10735863.title: RACIAL DIFFERENCES IN THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN SENSE OF CONTROL AND SOCIAL SUPPORT: A CROSS-LAGGED PANEL ANALYSIS
pmc-10735863.creator: Eunbea Kim, Gina Lee, Jeong Eun Lee
pmc-10735863.description: While it is widely acknowledged that having a sense of control and social support are crucial elements in promoting both physical and mental health among older adults, the relationship between these two factors and how they operate in diverse racial/ethnic settings is still unclear.

pmc-10811200.title: Current advances in biomaterials for inner ear cell regeneration
pmc-10811200.creator: Junze Lu, Man Wang, Yu Meng, Weibin An, Xue Wang, Gaoying Sun, Haibo Wang, Wenwen Liu
pmc-10811200.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Inner ear cell regeneration from stem/progenitor cells provides potential therapeutic strategies for the restoration of sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), however, the efficiency of regeneration is low and the functions of differentiated cells are not yet mature. Biomaterials have been used in inner ear cell regeneration to construct a more physiologically relevant 3D culture system which mimics the stem cell microenvironment and facilitates cellular interactions. Currently, these biomaterials include hydrogel, conductive materials, magneto-responsive materials, photo-responsive materials, etc.

pmc-11335624.title: The effect of sexual orientation on voice acoustic properties
pmc-11335624.creator: Luke Holmes, Gerulf Rieger, Silke Paulmann
pmc-11335624.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionPrevious research has investigated sexual orientation differences in the acoustic properties of individuals’ voices, often theorizing that homosexuals of both sexes would have voice properties mirroring those of heterosexuals of the opposite sex.

pmc-11455353.title: 7662 Mass Spectrometry Imaging Reveals Region-, Age-, And Sex-Specific Effects Of Lipopolysaccharide Administration On Glucocorticoids In Mouse Lymphoid Organs
pmc-11455353.creator: Melody Salehzadeh, Shazia Khan, Ruth Andrew, Kiran K Soma
pmc-11455353.description: Disclosure: M. Salehzadeh: None. S. Khan: None. R. Andrew: None. K.K. Soma: None.Glucocorticoids (GCs) are steroids that are critical for immune function. Immune organs, such as the thymus and spleen, locally produce GCs (i.e., immunosteroids). However, GC concentrations in the thymus and spleen at the cellular level, and how these levels are affected by stress, remain largely unknown.

pmc-11608245.title: A multicenter trial on the predictors of different subtypes of hemorrhagic infarction after thrombolysis
pmc-11608245.creator: Mohamed G. Zeinhom, Sherihan Rezk Ahmed, Ahmed Mohamed Kohail, Islam Fathallah Mohamed Kamel, ALshimaa Mahfouz Abdelrahman, Omar M. AL-Nozha, Mohamed Almoataz, Tarek Youssif Omar Youssif, Ahmed Mohamed Ali Daabis, Hossam Mohamed Refat, Ahmed Ahmed Mohamed Kamal Ebied, Ahmed Elbassiouny, Ahmed Zaki O
pmc-11608245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Worldwide, stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability in adults. Alteplase is the only approved treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and results in an improvement in a third of treated patients. Most studies evaluated the post-alteplase haemorrhagic transformation of brain infarction as a homogeneous entity but we evaluated the predictors of each subtype of haemorrhagic transformation of brain infarction. Our trial included 616 AIS alteplase-treated patients.

pmc-13378405.title: Distal cortical notching significantly decreases tibial stability following tibial tubercle osteotomy: An in vitro porcine biomechanical study
pmc-13378405.creator: Eiken Senkbeil, Kay Sellenschloh, Karl‐Heinz Frosch, Matthias Krause, Sara Checa, Jannik Frings
pmc-13378405.description: PurposeDistalizing tibial tubercle osteotomy (dTTO) is an effective treatment for patella alta, yet complications can be severe. This study evaluates the biomechanical effects of distal cut orientation on tibial fracture risk. It was hypothesised that orthogonal cutting and cortical notching reduce tibial stability.MethodsA total of 61 porcine tibiae were tested in three setups.

pmc-13447510.title: Single-cell analysis of microglia and monocyte dynamics uncovers distinct TNF-driven neuroimmune signatures in humans after intracerebral hemorrhage
pmc-13447510.creator: Yuki Kawamura, Conor W Johnson, Jonathan DeLong, Lucas Paulo de Lima Camillo, Sofia E Velazquez, Munetomo Takahashi, Hannah E Beatty, Ryan Hebert, Branden J Cord, Charles Matouk, Michael H Askenase, Lauren H Sansing
pmc-13447510.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Innate immune cells contribute to both secondary brain injury and repair following intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). However, the signaling pathways governing initial inflammatory and subsequent reparative myeloid programs in living patients remain poorly understood. To better characterize mononuclear phagocyte cell changes over time, we generated a single-cell transcriptomic dataset of paired hematoma clot evacuates and peripheral blood samples from 10 patients following ICH (5–290 h).

pmc-13545898.title: Amniotic membrane for oral surgical defect coverage: A clinical study
pmc-13545898.creator: Meenakshi Kothari, Satishkumar G. Patil, Ashwin Shah, Udupikrishna Joshi, Chaitanya Kothari
pmc-13545898.description: Reconstruction of oral soft-tissue defects remains limited by donor-site morbidity and inconsistent healing with currently available grafts. In this prospective interventional study, we assessed human amniotic membrane (HAM) as a biologically active scaffold in 15 patients (6 cleft alveolus, 2 oral submucous fibrosis, 7 vestibuloplasty; ages 8-65 years).

pmc-13582312.title: Longitudinal changes in pain catastrophizing and multidimensional health outcomes after passive-recharge burst spinal cord stimulation: a cohort study with follow-up to two years
pmc-13582312.creator: Johan Wänman, Jakob Östman, Pedram Tabatabaei
pmc-13582312.description: PurposeTo evaluate longitudinal changes in pain catastrophizing following spinal cord stimulation (SCS) and to determine whether baseline pain catastrophizing was associated with patient-reported outcomes over two years after implantation.MethodsA retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected data from 58 patients undergoing SCS implantation.
